💡 The novelty lies in using anion-dipole tailoring and directional dipole coordination to stabilize the LRMO cathode-electrolyte interface, suppressing Mn dissolution and anion hydrolysis-driven acid generation. 💡 The novelty lies in combining a thiourea-based porous organic polymer with carbon nanotubes as an interlayer, exploiting thiourea groups to chemically entrap lithium polysulfides. This addresses the shuttle effect, a key barrier to Li-S commercialization. The significance is enhanced sulfur utilization and cycling stability, offering a low-cost, earth-abundant route toward practical high-energy Li-S batteries.

Journal of Materials Chemistry A | 🔬 Research Article | 🔓 Open Access
💡 This study reveals how cation chemistry and cosolvent choice govern solvation nanostructure, ion transport, and interfacial kinetics in ionic liquid electrolytes—an underexplored fundamental gap. By linking molecular-level solvation organization to macroscopic transport and interfacial behavior, it provides design principles for high-voltage lithium metal batteries, enabling rational electrolyte engineering beyond empirical trial-and-error approaches.
